A_trait: nectariferous spur integrity and floral-larceny state
claim_ceiling: Same floral organ links legitimate pollination, larceny/florivory and fruit set, but the focal state is generated by consumers rather than an independent do(A)
decision_note: Frontiers full text reports three populations with distinct pollinator/thief/robber/florivore guilds and fruit-set; florivory of the spur dissuades pollinators whereas thieving/robbing can increase visits and fruit-set. Near-pass only because consumer damage/larceny, not an independently manipulated attraction coordinate, defines the contrast.

column27: Nine-year Aspidistra study establishes obligate pollination plus larval pollen parasitism by the same midge system, but it does not test a declared floral attraction/display coordinate A against pollinator and antagonist responses. Preserve as brood-pollination context, not a shared-cue test.

A_trait: floral tube/spur and openness trait complex
claim_ceiling: Floral access traits are associated with pollinator and cheater guilds and reveal a robber-versus-thief trade-off, but no common reproductive outcome or do(A) is present
decision_note: Open Ecosphere full text contains 14,391 visits across 195 plant species; pollinators, robbers and thieves share the community dataset, and specialized access traits that deter thieving are associated with greater robbing. This is comparative receiver-overlap evidence, not a fitness-linked experiment.

A_trait: corolla lower-lip structure and experimentally simulated corolla herbivory
claim_ceiling: Strict four-field coverage is satisfied: corolla structure was manipulated, pollinator response and fruit-predator visitation were measured, and reproductive output was measured. The antagonist response to the A manipulation was null, so this does not establish positive dual-audience conflict.
decision_note: Sánchez-Lafuente 2007 full text reports experimental lower-lip removal, reduced pollinator selection/successful visitation and lower fruit production, while no experimental treatment affected fruit-predator visitation. Count as strict linked measurement architecture, not as evidence that the manipulated A increased antagonist use.

column27: Brassica nigra herbivore treatments alter pollinator community composition, florivore performance and seed set, but the causal contrast is herbivore identity/induced plant state rather than a declared floral attraction/display coordinate A whose value is read by both audiences.

claim_ceiling: Cultivar corolla morphology predicts legitimate visitor identity/visitation and nectar-robbing behaviour, but no common plant reproductive outcome or randomized A manipulation is included.
decision_note: 2026 Web Ecology full text evaluates 19 cultivars in one field, links corolla morphology to major pollinators and percentage of flowers robbed, and provides a clean shared access-geometry near-pass without plant-fitness closure.

claim_ceiling: Both pollinators and nectar robbers prefer larger displays, robbery reduces reproductive output, and survey/experimental estimates converge on an overrepresented flower-number optimum; strict status is withheld because the common reproductive outcome is not one randomized A surface.
decision_note: American Naturalist source reports 109 plants over two years plus floral arrays: both pollinators and robbers preferred larger displays, robbery lowered reproduction, and the inferred optimum flower number was substantially overrepresented. Strong compromise/evolutionary-outcome evidence, but not promoted to strict common-W experiment.

claim_ceiling: Hadena consistently prefers longer corolla tubes and oviposition is positively associated with both fruit initiation and later flower/fruit predation; no randomized do(A), so this is linked dual-role evidence rather than strict causation.
decision_note: Kula et al. 2013 full text/primary abstract reports consistent long-corolla oviposition preference by the pollinating seed predator and both pollination-associated fruit initiation and larval predation consequences.

column27: Nine-population Silene-Hadena study is a comparative population-genetic analysis of host and dual-role pollinator/seed predator. It does not evaluate a declared floral attraction/display coordinate A or its receiver responses, so genetic co-structure alone is outside the one-trait gate.

claim_ceiling: Pollen alkaloids are measured against pollen thieves and legitimate pollinators; thieves show no relationship and lab Bombus responses are zero-compatible, while no plant reproductive outcome is linked to the same A contrast.
decision_note: Rivest et al. 2024 full text reports no relation between pollen alkaloids and pollen-thief abundance; plants with higher alkaloids received more but shorter pollinator visits with no overall flowers-visited change, and thermopsine-spiked pollen did not significantly alter Bombus behaviour. Near-pass with explicit null/zero-compatible channels.

column27: Pollinator visitation is analysed against flower density, whereas seed-predator foraging is analysed against seed density. Because the two audiences are not evaluated on the same declared floral coordinate A, opposite concentration/dilution responses cannot be used as a shared-cue test.

Silene-Hadena-Microbotryum study measures oviposition as a function of infection, flower/ovary traits and neighbourhood. The authors explicitly note that visitation patterns to healthy versus infected flowers had not been specifically studied, so a measured pollinator-response channel to the focal traits is absent.

Symphytum study shows nectar-robbing pressure and nectar removal trigger corolla abscission, which enhances self-pollination and seed set. The causal contrast is robber action causing a plant response, not a predeclared floral attraction/display A independently evaluated by pollinators and antagonists.

A_trait: floral morph and flower/leaf gelsemine concentration
claim_ceiling: Across five populations, floral morph/gelsemine expression is related to pollen receipt and nectar-robbing context, but no randomized A manipulation or common reproductive fitness surface is present.
decision_note: Irwin & Adler 2006 full text tests correlated pollination- and herbivore-resistance traits in five populations; floral/leaf gelsemine and morph affect pollination more strongly than robbing. Retain as observational shared-trait near-pass without fitness closure.

column27: Bumblebee study compares legitimate versus nectar-robbing handling tactics and their energetic efficiencies across bee-plant combinations. The focal contrast is animal foraging tactic, not a declared plant floral coordinate A evaluated by mutualist and antagonist receiver channels.

claim_ceiling: Mutualistic and antagonistic bird-flower subnetworks overlap and feeding behavior varies with flower size/plant origin, but no common plant reproductive outcome or experimental A contrast is available.
decision_note: Yoshikawa & Isagi 2014 full text separates 784 bird-flower feeding episodes into mutualistic and antagonistic subnetworks; flower size influences feeding behavior and some birds act as both pollinator and flower predator. Strong comparative receiver-overlap evidence without fitness closure.
